summary: Reactions puts a row of emoji reactions under a message, set up for an update the agent posted. People click a reaction to add or remove their own, or pick a new one from a small picker, and the counts roll up or down as they change. It gives the team a lightweight way to acknowledge or approve what the agent reported.
use: When an agent posts a status update in a chat thread and people want to acknowledge it
When a quick signal, such as a check or eyes, is enough and a reply would be noise
When the team should see at a glance who has reacted to an update
When you want an agent update to sit flat in a thread or stand alone as a card
features: Clicking a reaction toggles yours: its edge turns a stronger grey and its count takes the accent's text colour, the count rolls up, and it gets a small jump.
Removing the last reaction of a kind fades it out and shrinks it before it leaves the row.
The add button opens a picker of `emojis`; picking one you already have pulses it instead of counting twice.
Each reaction's tooltip names who reacted, like "You, Maya, Jon and 2 more", using `people` and `meLabel`.
Reactions that arrive after the first render pop in.
`bare` (the default) keeps it flat for a chat thread; set it to false to give it its own card.
a11y: Each reaction is a button with `aria-pressed` showing whether you reacted with it.
The add button has an `aria-label` and opens a `menu` of `menuitem` emoji, with `aria-expanded` on the trigger.
Escape closes the picker and returns focus to the add button.

From the keyboard, Enter, Space or the down arrow opens the picker on its first emoji; the arrow keys move through the grid (up and down a row at a time) and wrap, Home and End jump to the ends, and Tab closes it.
The tooltips naming who reacted use `role="tooltip"` and also open on keyboard focus.

faq.q: How do I keep reactions in sync with my backend?
faq.a: Control it with `reactions` and `onReactionsChange`. You get the full updated list after every toggle or pick, and can save it and pass back what the server returns.
A reaction with `mine: true`. Its `count` includes you, and the tooltip puts `meLabel`, "You" by default, before the names in `people`.

faq.q: Can I change the emoji in the picker?
faq.a: Yes. Pass `emojis` as an array of strings. Twelve common ones are the default.
